name: DBS Bank
summary: DBS says on its careers site that you may be asked scenario-based questions so it can learn about your values and working style, and that the number of interviews depends on the role. Candidates commonly report online or game-based assessments for graduate roles, then interviews with the hiring team, and for some technology roles DBS has hired through hackathons. DBS's PRIDE! values (Purpose-driven, Relationship-led, Innovative, Decisive and Everything Fun) are a good guide to what interviewers listen for.
rounds: Online assessments for some roles, such as problem-solving games or a coding test
Interview with a hiring team member about your experience, with scenario-based questions
Further interviews, sometimes a panel, a presentation or a case for some roles

questions.text: Tell me about a time you made a decision quickly without all the information you wanted.
covers: What was at stake and the time pressure
What you knew, what you assumed, and how you decided
The outcome and what you'd do again

questions.text: Tell me about a relationship with a client or colleague that you turned around.
covers: What had gone wrong
What you did to rebuild trust
Where the relationship ended up

questions.text: Tell me about a time you used technology or data to improve how something was done.
covers: The old way and its cost
The tool or data you used and how
The measurable improvement

questions.text: Tell me about a setback and how you bounced back.
covers: What happened and how it felt
What you did next
What you learned

questions.text: A customer is angry that a payment didn't reach a supplier on time. What do you do?
covers: Listening and acknowledging the impact
Finding out what happened and what can be done now
Following up and preventing a repeat

questions.text: How would you make a branch or call-centre process digital without leaving older customers behind?
covers: Who uses it today and why
A digital path plus support for those who need it
How you'd measure adoption and satisfaction

questions.text: You spot a transaction pattern that looks like money laundering. What do you do?
covers: Not tipping off the customer
Escalating through the right compliance channel
Recording what you saw clearly

questions.text: How would you explain a fixed deposit versus a mutual fund to a first-time investor?
covers: Risk and return in plain words
Liquidity and time horizon
Asking about their goals before recommending

questions.text: How would you prioritise three urgent requests from different stakeholders on the same day?
covers: Clarifying impact and deadlines
Agreeing order with the people involved
Communicating what will slip and when

questions.text: Which of DBS's PRIDE! values fits you best, and when did you show it?
covers: The value and why you chose it
A specific example
What it achieved

questions.text: Why do you want to join DBS?
covers: Something specific about DBS's direction or customers
How your experience fits the role
What you hope to build there

questions.text: Where do you see yourself growing in banking or technology over the next few years?
covers: A direction grounded in the role
Skills you'll build
How DBS fits that path

tips: Prepare a short story for each PRIDE! value: purpose-driven, relationship-led, innovative, decisive and everything fun.
Expect scenario questions ('what would you do if…'); answer with what you'd actually do first, second and third.
Ask your Talent Advisor what to bring and how many interviews to expect; DBS says it varies by role.
For technology roles, practise coding tests; DBS has also used hackathons to hire developers.

sources.title: DBS: Hack2Hire, hiring developers through a hackathon
